assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Fully displayed formula
items.clue: A drawing showing every atom and every bond.

items.label: Alkene
items.clue: A hydrocarbon with a carbon-carbon double bond.

items.label: Unsaturated
items.clue: Describes a molecule able to take on more atoms by addition.

items.label: Molecular formula
items.clue: Gives the number of atoms of each element in one particle, such as C3H6.

questions.stem: What is the general formula for the homologous series of alkenes?

options.text: CₙH₂ₙ — twice as many hydrogen atoms as carbon atoms
CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ — two hydrogen atoms more than twice the carbon
CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ — two hydrogen atoms fewer than twice the carbons
CₙHₙ — one hydrogen atom for every carbon atom present

questions.explanation: The specification gives CₙH₂ₙ for the alkenes: propene is C₃H₆ and butene is C₄H₈.

questions.stem: Which of these is a correct description of an alkene?

options.text: A hydrocarbon in which every carbon bond is a single bond
A hydrocarbon containing a carbon–carbon double bond
A compound of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen atoms
A hydrocarbon made unreactive by its double bond

questions.explanation: Alkenes are hydrocarbons with a double carbon-carbon bond, as the specification states.

questions.stem: Propane has the formula C₃H₈. What is the formula of propene?

options.text: C₃H₄, which is four hydrogen atoms fewer than propane
C₃H₆, two hydrogen atoms fewer than propane
C₃H₈, exactly the same formula as propane has
C₃H₇, one hydrogen atom fewer than propane has

questions.explanation: An alkene has two fewer hydrogen atoms than the alkane with the same number of carbon atoms.

questions.stem: Why is propene described as unsaturated?

options.text: It has two hydrogen atoms fewer than propane does
It has four hydrogen atoms fewer than propane does
Every bond between its carbon atoms is a single bond
Each carbon atom is joined to as many atoms as it can be

questions.explanation: The specification defines unsaturated in exactly this way: two fewer hydrogen atoms than the alkane with the same number of carbon atoms.

questions.stem: Which list gives the first four members of the homologous series of alkenes?

options.text: Methene, ethene, propene and pentene
Ethene, ethane, butene and butane
Ethene, propene, butene and pentene
Ethene, propene, butene and hexene

questions.explanation: These are the four members named in the specification.

questions.stem: What does the molecular formula C₃H₆ tell you about a propene molecule?

options.text: The number of atoms of each element in the molecule
Where the double bond lies and how the atoms join
Only the ratio of carbon to hydrogen atoms present
Every bond in the molecule, shown drawn out

questions.explanation: A molecular formula gives the actual count of each kind of atom: three carbon and six hydrogen.

questions.stem: Which of these formulae fits the general formula CₙH₂ₙ?

options.text: C₄H₁₀
C₂H₅OH
CH₃COOH
C₃H₆

questions.explanation: Six hydrogen atoms for three carbon atoms is 2n hydrogen atoms, so this fits the alkenes.

questions.stem: Propene can also be drawn as a fully displayed formula. What does that show that C₃H₆ does not?

options.text: Nothing new; the same information is drawn out
Only how many atoms of each element are present
Every atom and every bond, including the double bond
How the molecules are arranged in a sample of propene

questions.explanation: A displayed formula sets out each bond, so the position of the C=C can be seen.
